title: Changing keys and playing in difficult keys
summary: Discussion of musicians struggling with key changes; Smith's Janis band transposed deliberately and he explains how difficult keys alter playing.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: well even the best ones sometimes get confused when they have to change keys things like that they're not used to playing something in a
I've seen that happen to Jimmy Darcy who must have had every kind of experience imaginable as a young man and playing and he couldn't get together with the Dukes of Dixon and he had any kind of keys

now that's odd because even my limited experience we always played in all kinds of keys with the Conrad Janus band just for exercise we used to deliberately change keys or transpose in the middle of tunes just to you get a very different flavor out of a tune when you play it in a different key because I can't explain how it happens but you just get a very different feeling I tell you you get in a very difficult key you start playing in D flat

going to start playing a little bit simpler to begin with and you might kind of get on a more basic driving thing because your fingers just aren't glib in that key the more you play in it of course the more you're going to be glib but you're going to be glib in that key and a lot of the patterns that are going to come out are going to be very different than if you were playing in E flat or B flat easier trumpet keys
